def: A 64-bit pointer to a location inside one memory page, used by NVMe over PCIe to describe where a command's data lives. PRP1 may have an offset; every later data entry is page aligned.

An array of 8-byte page-aligned PRP entries in host memory, pointed to by PRP2 when a transfer crosses more than one memory page boundary. When more entries remain than fit in the list page, its last slot points to the next list page.
SQE Dwords 6-9 (16 bytes): either PRP1 and PRP2, or SGL Entry 1, depending on PSDT.
SQE Dwords 4-5: the address of a contiguous metadata buffer, or of an SGL segment describing metadata when PSDT is 10b.

exp: PRP or SGL for Data Transfer
def: Command Dword 0 bits 15:14. 00b selects PRPs; 01b and 10b select SGLs (differing in how MPTR is interpreted); 11b is reserved.
A chain of 16-byte descriptors (address, length, type) describing a command's data or metadata buffer. Optional for I/O on NVMe over PCIe; required on NVMe over Fabrics.
An SGL descriptor that describes Length bytes of data at Address, with no page-alignment rules.
A contiguous array of SGL descriptors in memory, reached through a Segment (type 2h) or Last Segment (type 3h) descriptor, which may only be the last descriptor of the preceding segment.
An SGL descriptor telling the controller to discard Length bytes of read data instead of transferring them to host memory. Optional; advertised in SGLS.
An SGL descriptor with an address, a 24-bit length and a 32-bit remote memory key, used by NVMe over RDMA.
Identify Controller field reporting whether SGLs are supported (bits 1:0: 00b no, 01b yes, 10b yes with dword alignment) and which optional descriptor types and features are supported.
The address a device puts on the bus when an IOMMU translates DMA; the IOMMU maps it to a physical address and checks permissions per device.
The page size the controller uses to interpret PRP entries: 2^(12 + CC.MPS) bytes, within CAP.MPSMIN to CAP.MPSMAX. Unrelated to PCIe Max Payload Size.
Identify Controller field limiting one command's data transfer to 2^MDTS units of the minimum memory page size; 0 means no limit is reported.
